question: Which of the following plant tissues is made up of cells that are dead at maturity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a simple permanent plant tissue characterized by cells that are **dead at maturity**. These cells lose their **protoplasm** during development, leaving behind only the cell wall. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The cell walls of **sclerenchyma** are significantly thickened due to the deposition of **lignin**, a complex polymer that acts as a waterproof cementing material.
 
• Due to the extreme thickness of the **lignified** walls, there are no **intercellular spaces** between the cells, making the tissue very dense and rigid.
 
• The primary **function** of **sclerenchyma** is to provide **mechanical strength** and structural rigidity to the plant, allowing it to withstand environmental stresses like wind and weight.
 
• This tissue is commonly found in the **stems** (around vascular bundles), in the **veins of leaves**, and in the **hard coverings** of seeds and nuts, such as the shell of a **coconut**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma**:
 
 
• This is the most fundamental and abundant simple tissue in plants. The cells are **living** with thin cell walls made of **cellulose**.
 
• They possess large **central vacuoles** and are involved in **photosynthesis**, **storage** of food, and **secretion**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma**:
 
 
• This tissue consists of **living cells** that are elongated and have **unevenly thickened** cell walls, particularly at the corners.
 
• The thickening is due to the deposition of **cellulose**, **hemicellulose**, and **pectin**. It provides **flexibility** and mechanical support to young growing parts like the **petiole** of a leaf. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Aerenchyma**:
 
 
• It is a specialized type of **parenchyma** found in **hydrophytes** (aquatic plants).
 
• It contains large **air cavities** or spaces that facilitate the exchange of gases and provide **buoyancy** to the plant, helping it float. Since it is a parenchyma variant, its cells are **living**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Sclerenchyma**:
 
 
• **Fibers**: These are long, narrow, and thick-walled cells with **tapering ends**. They usually occur in bundles and are used commercially in making **ropes** and **textiles** (e.g., **jute** and **hemp**).
 
• **Sclereids**: Also known as **stone cells**, these are spherical or oval cells with extremely thick walls and very narrow **lumens**. They are responsible for the **gritty texture** found in fruits like **pears** and **sapota**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Composition**:
 
 
• The presence of **lignin** is a key distinguishing **feature** of sclerenchyma compared to collenchyma (which uses pectin) and parenchyma (which uses thin cellulose). **Lignification** is the process that eventually leads to the death of the **protoplast**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison**:
 
 
• While **Xylem** (a complex tissue) also contains dead cells like **tracheids** and **vessels** for water transport, **sclerenchyma** is the primary **simple permanent tissue** dedicated solely to **mechanical protection**.
